links.citation: Mark Bell: MBV was "hugely influential on the bass sound... We had become addicted to noise."

Bell, MusicRadar: "We were basically translating our version of a certain crop of 60s bands... and putting that through a filter of what was going on right then. The Mary Chain, the Valentines, the House Of Love and Spacemen 3."
Mark Bell, Premier Guitar: "you can easily tell when it was we'd heard Sonic Youth, because we immediately started to employ noise techniques... Songs like 'Nowhere' and 'Seagull' came out of that."
Bell, Under the Radar: "Early on in Ride, it was Spacemen 3, House of Love, My Bloody Valentine, Loop, Sonic Youth, Dinosaur Jr., The Fall, Pixies, and Stone Roses."
Andy Bell to Under the Radar: "Early on in Ride, it was Spacemen 3, House of Love, My Bloody Valentine, Loop, Sonic Youth, Dinosaur Jr., The Fall, Pixies, and Stone Roses."

Rolling Stone, on writing Psychocandy: "we got seriously into the Velvets and the Stooges."
Rolling Stone: "The bands that didn't make us want to puke back then were the likes of the Birthday Party or Echo and the Bunnymen."
MOJO's oral history of the band, Lou Barlow: "J loved The Zombies and Neil Young."

OMD Wikipedia bio: Kraftwerk was OMD's "primary musical influence"; McCluskey credits Autobahn with piquing his and Humphreys' interest in electronic music; "Electricity" described as "a punky sped-up version of Kraftwerk's Radioactivity."
Paul Westerberg picked "Judy Is a Punk" in a 2004 radio interview -- a favorites-tier pick, not a stated influence claim.

Justin Trosper, Piero Scaruffi interview (1999): "more influenced by the DC punk thing happening back then... (husker du/black flag/mission of burma)"; Fugazi also named directly in the band's general influences list (AllMusic/Fred Thomas).
Justin Trosper, Piero Scaruffi interview (1999): "more influenced by... US hardcore (husker du/black flag/mission of burma)."

Klaus Dinger in Uncut's "lost" Neu! interview, recorded in 2000 around the reissues: "Velvet Underground was in there. Also The Beatles, several years before, like Michael said, also The Stones, all the big ones I would say." Michael Rother adds only "That was in the background too, yeah" -- first-person, but an acknowledgement of background listening rather than a claim about shaping Neu!'s sound, hence the lowered confidence.
Nick Cave told the German magazine Spex in 2013 that David Bowie was his idol, and that he owned all of Bowie's early albums along with the three Berlin records.
Red Hand Files, issue #16: Cohen's "Avalanche" ranks first on Nick Cave's own list of ten favorite pieces of music by other artists.

Michael Gira, Pitchfork interview republished at younggodrecords.com (May 19, 2014): asked about influences, named "Nina Simone, James Brown, Fela Kuti, Can, and Led Zeppelin."
"SWANS: Where Does a Body End?" (YouTube, Sept 9, 2023): Michael Gira named Suicide as an influence.

Michael Gira told The Line of Best Fit that early Glenn Branca concerts were "just the epitome of how high music can go," describing the soaring, ever-ascending sound of them as "really inspirational."
